questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can you have before your driving is affected?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: What is one way to practice defensive driving?

options.text: Scan the road ahead.
Rubberneck.
Stare straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Good defensive driving means staying alert and scanning the road ahead. This lets you see hazards early and gives you time to react safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop and look both ways before entering, unless a police officer directs you otherwise.

questions.question: Which of these affects how fast your body absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Body weight, biological sex, food in your stomach, and the number of drinks consumed all affect how your body absorbs alcohol. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: When driving on a one-way street, when can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you speed up before the turn.
When traffic on that street moves to the right.
When traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left, unless a sign says you cannot. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: If another car is following you too closely on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to match the other car's speed.
Move to the right lane and let the other car pass.
Slow down to bother the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane and let the other car pass.
questions.explanation: If you are being tailgated in the left lane, move to the right lane to let the other car pass. The left lane is for faster traffic passing slower vehicles.

questions.question: What color and shape are construction zone signs?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the highway is divided.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will be slippery when wet and harder to control.

questions.question: Which of these is dangerous in a work zone?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely.
Not watching for workers and moving equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and machines.

questions.question: What should a driver always do about the right-of-way?

options.text: Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Always watch the situation at an intersection. Yield the right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
Speed does not affect them.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The maximum speed limit in good conditions is 55 mph.
You must not drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit in good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the highest legal speed. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: How do strong wind gusts affect highway driving?

options.text: Generally affect only the movement of large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers. It reduces visibility by blowing dust and dirt onto the road. It can also physically push your vehicle off course.

questions.question: Even a small amount of alcohol in the blood may affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can harm your judgment and coordination. Even small amounts can make it unsafe to drive and can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: What does safe interstate driving require?

options.text: Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.
Be constantly alert.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Interstate highways require you to stay alert at all times and drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: Texting while driving makes you ____ times more likely to crash than a non-distracted driver.

options.text: Five

questions.explanation: Texting while driving makes you 20 times more likely to crash. Reading or writing a text takes your eyes off the road for about 4.6 seconds. At 55 mph, that is like driving the length of a football field with your eyes closed.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Even with proper mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: If you see a single broken white line on a highway, you:

options.text: Cannot cross the line to pass.
May cross the line to pass and change lanes.
May only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: May cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross a white dashed line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. Wait until the gate is raised and you can see clearly in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: What does excessive speed often lead to?

options.text: Does not increase the chance of a crash.
Increases your ability to react to a hazard.
Often leads to high-risk decision-making.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to high-risk decision-making.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a common cause of crashes. It does not save time and often causes drivers to make risky decisions.

questions.question: How should you enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check behind and to the side of your vehicle to make sure the lane is clear.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before the turn. Keep your front wheels straight ahead until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another vehicle hits you from behind.
